distinctions_drawn: strict law vs. ceteris paribus generalization
explicit_definitions_given: disease as internal dysfunction interfering with normal function
anomalous monism as token identity without type identity
explanatory autonomy as non-replaceable patterns without ontological independence

objections_raised: Davidson's charity makes mental illness impossible
Klee's ceteris paribus objection undermines strict law contrast
No strict laws undermines prediction and treatment

philosophical_orientation.grounding: analytic philosophy of mind and medicine
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: mental health, reductionism, anomalous monism, biological dysfunction, explanatory autonomy

summary_of_core_decisions: The text defends a middle position: Boorse's physiological model is compatible with Davidson's anomalous monism if disease is understood as biological grounding rather than strict psychological reduction; mental-health science can be autonomous only in an explanatory/methodological sense, not ontologically or nomologically.
